scenes.title: How a missile over Yemen can hit an Indian household
scenes.say: A missile over Yemen can seem far away. Here's how it can reach an Indian household.

scenes.label: Brent crude on 22 October: its highest close since 4 May
scenes.say: On 22 October, Brent crude closed at $113.17 a barrel, its highest since May, on fears of Middle East supply disruption.
scenes.speak: On the twenty-second of October, Brent crude closed at a hundred and thirteen dollars a barrel, its highest since May, on fears of Middle East supply disruption.

scenes.title: Two narrow waters, one big risk
scenes.say: Two chokepoints matter. Hormuz, for Gulf oil and gas. And Bab el-Mandeb, the gateway to the Red Sea and Suez, for trade with Europe.

scenes.title: How the shock travels
scenes.say: No blockade is needed. The threat alone makes ships reroute and insurers raise premiums. Oil costs more, and a weaker rupee makes it worse.

scenes.title: The long way round
items: Around the Cape of Good Hope
scenes.say: Ships avoiding the Red Sea sail round the Cape of Good Hope. That means more fuel, more time, fewer free ships and higher freight for Indian exporters.

scenes.text: Sometimes the threat of disruption is enough to make every barrel more expensive.
scenes.say: India imports most of its crude. So sometimes, the threat of disruption is enough to make every barrel more expensive.

scenes.title: What India should do
scenes.say: India's answer: bigger strategic reserves, more suppliers and routes, protection for shipping and seafarers, resilient logistics, and a push for de-escalation.
